regions.summary: Unpack the two input BCD bytes at $2F/$30 into four low-first decimal digits, zero the remaining two addend digits, and add into the six unpacked score digits at $04DE. Carry is implemented explicitly because the NES has no decimal arithmetic; overflow beyond digit six is discarded. F1E1 selects physical PRG banks 0/1 for this call; the same CPU address in PRG pair six is a different routine.

units.summary: Add A to the decimal pair at $04C6/$04C7. Carry past 99 increments the shared saturated pair at $04C4/$04C5. The neighboring entry points increment, decrement or add to other decimal pairs; callers supply small decimal addends, not arbitrary binary bytes.

regions.summary: Little-endian descriptor pointers indexed by the PRG pair zero upload loader. The first cell is null. Twenty pointed seven-byte descriptors are supported; the last apparent pointer reaches executable palette code and is not a valid extra descriptor. Seven-byte records contain bank, two-byte output length, source pointer and optional two-byte PPU destination. The fixed upload loader reads these fields; adjacent records end at independently established palette code. This physical emission may be a slice of an overlapping consumer footprint; its boundary does not imply a separate original resource.

Zero tiles still consume source bytes; this differs from the ordinary sprite grid format.

regions.summary: Advance the scene command cursor. An inactive command returns; active commands select a two-byte record through $11, using either the saved index or the advancing cursor. The top two bits choose strip, scene-control or object-control updates. Strip records set or XOR one flag byte, locate the descriptor group through $05, synchronize with the frame consumer and continue into strip generation. Valid descriptor indices and map coordinates are local calling preconditions.

Valid descriptor indices and map coordinates are local calling preconditions.

units.name: ChooseSceneStripReplacement
units.summary: Return a replacement map byte in A and tile/attribute value in Y for the current strip cell. Horizontal and vertical cases use the command direction bits, old tile class and original flag bits to select empty, special terrain or alternate cells. The long decision tree is a finite tile policy, not a general decoder; the individual terrain IDs retain mechanical names where game meaning is unknown.

units.name: ChooseVerticalPrimaryCell
units.summary: Clear the high map flag and choose special replacements for terrain pairs and alternating X parity. The previous map flag controls whether an attribute value is emitted.

Horizontal and vertical cases use the command direction bits, old tile class and original flag bits to select empty, special terrain or alternate cells. The long decision tree is a finite tile policy, not a general decoder; the individual terrain IDs retain mechanical names where game meaning is unknown.

units.name: ChooseVerticalClearCell
units.summary: Clear the high map flag and emit empty or unflagged terrain replacements; special terrain classes retain matching attributes.

regions.summary: Choose the overlay palette/layout from the signed overlay selector, clear the attribute buffer and edit-state counters, and draw the selectable character grid. Paired pointer tables supply the expected and editable strings; their high-bit terminator is cleared after copying into RAM. Center the resulting length in a 32-column row, queue its upload, initialize selection state and enter the existing overlay loop. These CPU aliases are physical banks 8/9, independent of the same numeric addresses in other banks.

Otherwise toggle row state or interpret Select/A/Start actions, wrap left/right cursor within the current item count, redraw it, and swap entries while selection is latched. regions.summary: Load this slot stream and interpret frame/duration pairs or commands $80..$B0. Three-byte command descriptors supply a handler word and exact parameter count; parameters are copied before dispatch, so the saved cursor points to the next token. Result zero continues immediately, $FF yields with timer one, and other results become the timer. Command $8D/$8C uses one overwritten return slot; $91/$90 uses one overwritten absolute loop pointer and eight-bit count. Predicate-based continuation requires preservation of script base/cursor, return/loop fields and effective pair six, beyond saving X/Y alone. Family-changing $9A/$9D entries install their own cursors; no universal recursive preservation or natural script entry is assumed.

Pack full X divided by eight with Y and area, then invalidate an older record whose area matches the current area's small equivalence chain. Carry set reports unavailable counter; carry clear reports a recorded position.

units.name: ConsumeCounterAndRecordPosition
units.summary: Require a nonzero bounded counter, then shift history, pack current coordinates and mark the history update. Return carry set if unavailable.

A separate retargeting policy picks one of 32 position/velocity triples, rejects the player's coarse quadrant, then moves along an axis once aligned with the player. Timer and random branches control the changes; original object identities remain unresolved.

units.name: BounceObjectWithinVerticalBand
units.summary: Reverse vertical velocity at Y limits $18/$C0 or when the leading vertical probe hits one of five terrain IDs.

phase1.evidence: R002-bank-return-continuations. Supported finite handlers and explicit restoring/CHR-only contracts; static entry preconditions per proposal-preconditions.json. No natural reachability or unrestricted selector assertion.

units.summary: Connected object handlers apply side/top probes, bounded vertical bouncing, four-point terrain sampling and timed action transitions. A separate retargeting policy picks one of 32 position/velocity triples, rejects the player's coarse quadrant, then moves along an axis once aligned with the player. Timer and random branches control the changes; original object identities remain unresolved.

units.name: RetargetObjectAcrossPlayerQuadrant
units.summary: For objects outside the base coordinate pages, periodically choose one of 32 packed positions and velocity pairs. Accept a candidate only when its coarse quadrant differs from the player's.

Subsequent entries initialize the display, palettes/upload state, nametables, frame waits and five-bit mapper serial writes. Mapper register values are not physical bank identities.

phase1.evidence: Actual immutable ROM opcode fetch in bounded title/intro/gameplay scenarios; PartIII buffer-patched scenarios are artificial, not natural reachability, exact effective CPU mapping from analysis/round-001/*contexts.json; independently decoded before annotation. Replay scripts and captures retained.

Subsequent entries initialize the display, palettes/upload state, nametables, frame waits and five-bit mapper serial writes. Mapper register values are not physical bank identities.

phase1.evidence: Actual immutable ROM opcode fetch in bounded title/intro/gameplay scenarios; PartIII buffer-patched scenarios are artificial, not natural reachability, exact effective CPU mapping from analysis/round-001/*contexts.json; independently decoded before annotation. Replay scripts and captures retained.

Packed dimensions control row/column traversal, $FF skips empty tiles, facing mirrors X traversal and attributes; offscreen tiles are clipped using high bytes.

units.name: RunGameplayHooksAndInteractions
units.summary: The first frame pass updates player input/terrain and object handlers, switches to PRG pair two for scene effects, then restores PRG pair six. The second pass services interaction tiles, scene timers, palettes, contact effects, support and object scripts before committing uploads and saving prior player coordinates/input. NMI-side helpers write state-run bytes, read seven PPU sample pairs and read or commit the pending attribute byte. Object overlap handling selects special player states or the shared failure path; tile $22 records its area bit and freezes object updates. Each bank switch shown is explicit; indirect callees retain unresolved bank contracts.

Cases include random facing changes, signed horizontal strip motion and latch changes for special terrain. A reset helper clears the support index sentinel three; another restores sampled ground height for selected tile IDs. Selectors and valid map coordinates remain local Static preconditions.

units.summary: Finite terrain-selected player handlers test neighboring cells and choose state transitions, vertical alignment or attachment. Cases include random facing changes, signed horizontal strip motion and latch changes for special terrain. Cases include random facing changes, signed horizontal strip motion and latch changes for special terrain. A reset helper clears the support index sentinel three; another restores sampled ground height for selected tile IDs. Selectors and valid map coordinates remain local Static preconditions.

units.name: ResolvePlayerAboveGround
units.summary: Clear the special latch and restore ground for the accepted terrain IDs. Otherwise inspect height/state and side terrain, clear the transition latch on alignment or continue into the previously reviewed response.

phase1.evidence: Supported hook/password/inventory callback entry and exact decoded static control flow; explicit bank-setting wrappers and conservative callee return-bank proof. analysis/round-002/static-review.json. Natural reachability unresolved.

regions.summary: Read three vertical sample points on each side of the player; obstructing tile IDs restore the prior horizontal coordinate.

units.name: SamplePlayerSidesAndAlignToTerrain
units.summary: Align the player to an eight-pixel vertical boundary when contact permits, clear motion state and start tile animation. Sample three heights on each side and restore prior X when terrain IDs $0E/$11/$12 obstruct motion. The common bounds helper derives top/middle/bottom sample points; the reader converts pixels to RAM row/column, returns tile $0E outside columns 0..27 and masks valid map cells to six bits.

units.name: SamplePlayerSidesAndAlignToTerrain
units.summary: Align the player to an eight-pixel vertical boundary when contact permits, clear motion state and start tile animation. Sample three heights on each side and restore prior X when terrain IDs $0E/$11/$12 obstruct motion. regions.summary: 32 split low/high row pointers indexed by the sampler after three right shifts. Rows 4..23 point to twenty RAM rows; the exact sequence includes $01B8 then $0200, so it is not a uniform-stride array. Other rows select the ROM sentinel at CPU $E3BC. Map writes require a RAM row and valid horizontal coordinates; unrestricted sampler input does not prove that precondition.

A world-coordinate helper switches banks and clips bounds. The object loop snaps falling objects to flat/slope ground or removes them for flagged terrain. The policy/slope bytes beginning $F851 are Data in the current map; their semantic split and full selector domains remain unresolved.

A world-coordinate helper switches banks and clips bounds. The object loop snaps falling objects to flat/slope ground or removes them for flagged terrain. The policy/slope bytes beginning $F851 are Data in the current map; their semantic split and full selector domains remain unresolved.

phase1.evidence: Actual immutable ROM opcode fetch in bounded natural title/intro/gameplay scenarios, exact effective CPU mapping from analysis/round-001/*contexts.json; independently decoded before annotation. Replay scripts and captures retained.

phase1.evidence: Actual immutable ROM opcode fetch in bounded natural title/intro/gameplay scenarios, exact effective CPU mapping from analysis/round-001/*contexts.json; independently decoded before annotation. Replay scripts and captures retained.

Walk the rectangular tile grid in eight-pixel steps, omitting zero tiles from OAM, then walk emitted records backwards to assign the final attribute byte. Restore the incoming PRG bank and return A=1. X is the caller's OAM byte cursor; capacity and record validity are caller preconditions.

units.name: SampleAreaCounterByFrame
units.summary: Use the descending frame byte to sample state entries: only ticks below $30 are eligible, masked with $2F, excluding the two active area selectors. Increment the sampled low nibble toward five and set its high flag. The game meaning of this per-area counter is unresolved.

units.name: LoadAndFadePalettes
units.summary: A and X select two 16-byte palettes through pointer tables; combine them into the 32-byte working palette and initialize the split-screen colors. The following entries preserve target colors and animate brightness/emphasis.

units.name: IntegrateObjectPositions
units.summary: Integrate eight object slots unless disabled or inactive. Signed velocities contribute an integer displacement plus three fractional bits, carried through separate position bytes. Temporarily add the shared X bias to slot zero, then remove it and clear the bias after the pass.

units.name: RunSelectOverlay
units.summary: Select bit $20 opens the bank-2 overlay. Initialize its three selectors, service frames until Select is released, then advance the vertical transition. This classified fragment ends before the rest of the close sequence.

units.name: OverlayReturn
units.summary: Shared return for the overlay paths, including the separately named menu callbacks and their release-wait continuation.

units.name: AdvanceOverlayScroll
units.summary: Service frames while adding four to the signed vertical position until it becomes nonnegative; finish at zero.

units.name: ServiceOverlayFrame
units.summary: Update palette and audio, wait for NMI acknowledgement, allow a bounded delay, then process overlay uploads, draw its contents and perform the raster split. Uses PRG register value two on return from bank wrappers.

units.name: InitializeOverlaySelectors
units.summary: Clear overlay scratch and derive three selectors from the saved status bytes, using seven for empty entries. The next entry builds two adjacent upload rows from descriptor tables.

units.name: DrawOverlayContents
units.summary: On alternate frames, queue the three selected overlay records and status digits, or a separate record for the other overlay mode. The classified suffix stops before that mode finishes.

units.name: OverlayDrawReturn
units.summary: Return target shared by the overlay draw paths.

units.name: PasswordScreenFrame
units.summary: Delay, then handle password-screen pending flags and blink a palette entry every sixteen frame ticks. The missing branches between classified fragments are intentionally retained as unknown.

units.name: PasswordScreenSecondFlag
units.summary: Continue the password state dispatcher after its first pending flag. The nonzero branch is not classified here.

units.name: CheckPasswordAcceptance
units.summary: Count down the acceptance delay, or compare the entered password when the input state allows it. A successful comparison requests sound $31, records success, and starts a thirty-frame delay.

units.name: PasswordFrameReturn
units.summary: Return without changing the password transition flag.

units.name: FinishPasswordDelay
units.summary: Set the transition request when the password acceptance countdown expires.

units.name: ComparePasswordBuffers
units.summary: Compare entered and expected buffers from index zero to the stored length. Returns A=1 on full equality and A=0 after saving the two mismatch indices. The buffers are loaded from the paired password records documented below.

units.name: AnimateTwoFramePalette
units.summary: Choose a four-byte phase from frame bit one and update palette entries. The duplicate write to the second entry is present in the original bytes.

units.name: AnimateScenePalette
units.summary: Dispatch on scene ID to palette effects: scene seven alternates colors every sixteen frames, eight changes colors with scroll position, twelve uses a two-frame effect, and fourteen returns. Scene six switches CHR state and continues into two alternate rectangle draws with a three-phase palette cycle.

units.name: ScenePaletteReturn
units.summary: Scene fourteen currently performs no palette work.

units.name: UpdateAudioSlotsLow
units.summary: Update active audio slots zero through three, then slots four through seven at the next entry. Load interpreter scratch, advance the stream, and write the scratch state back to the indexed slot.

units.name: AudioCommandThreeParameter
units.summary: Command three reads its repeat-target byte, saves that as the next stream cursor, reads the repeat counter and resumes the common command loop.

units.name: AudioCommandThreeCountdown
units.summary: On command-three expiration, decrement the repeat counter and skip the three-byte command before resuming the common stream loop.

units.name: DecodeAudioEvents
units.summary: Negative event bytes choose an eight-byte instrument descriptor; $FF returns to the command stream, zero silences a channel, and positive values select notes. Packed duration flags control tie/modulation behavior before the next timed update.

units.name: AudioTimedUpdate
units.summary: Wait-count processing updates timer-low registers with optional modulation/vibrato and respects the upper-slot ownership mask. Subsequent entries stop/start hardware channels and program pulse, triangle, or noise registers from the instrument and pitch tables.

units.name: UpdateAudioRequestUpper
units.summary: An upper-group request with bit seven initializes stream bases, tempo and four slots. Otherwise apply its frame divider and advance the upper group. A zero request starts releasing owned channels; that cleanup tail is not fully classified.

units.name: UpdateAudioRequestLower
units.summary: Initialize or tick the lower four audio slots using separate stream bases and tempo. If no request remains, clear those slots and disable their channels subject to upper-group ownership.

units.name: InitializeObjectAndScripts
units.summary: Mark an object inactive only once, or initialize an allocated slot from the spawn staging fields. Resolve its resource, clear per-slot state, select its script pointer table and start the chosen script. The later entry searches slots and decodes a packed three-byte spawn record.

units.name: UpdateObjectScripts
units.summary: Reset the allocation inhibit and scan eight slots. Active, unfrozen objects execute their script when its timer expires; each timer then decrements. A preceding pass arbitrates pending script changes by priority.

units.name: InterpretObjectScript
units.summary: The arbitration tail clears pending selectors. The interpreter reads a normal frame/timer pair or a high-bit command. Commands use three-byte descriptors (handler pointer and parameter count), copy parameters to scratch, then dispatch indirectly and resume or yield according to the result.

units.name: SelectObjectScript
units.summary: Change the current script only if it differs and the supplied priority is sufficient. Resolve a two-byte pointer in the object's script table; a zero high byte leaves the previous stream intact. Return with Y at the interpreter cursor.

units.name: SetObjectCommandField
units.summary: Script command copies its first parameter into a per-object field used by terrain processing. Its broader game meaning remains unresolved.

units.name: RequestUpperAudioFromScript
units.summary: Submit the first script parameter as an upper-group audio request, then restore the current object index.

units.name: RandomScriptBranch
units.summary: Rotate the random result and compare with the command threshold. Below threshold, jump to the script pointer supplied by the following two parameters; otherwise return.

units.name: YieldOrSetVelocityMode
units.summary: First entry returns the command result that controls interpreter yield. The following entry sets bit seven of the palette selector/control field before entering the facing-selected shared tail; its broader action meaning remains tentative.

units.name: SetObjectVelocity
units.summary: Assign vertical velocity and choose whether horizontal velocity must be negated from the object's facing flag. The facing-selected tail continues through the shared indexed field helper.

units.name: SetMirroredOrVerticalVelocity
units.summary: Negate the horizontal script parameter for mirrored objects. A separate entry sets that control bit and assigns the vertical velocity parameter.

units.name: SetObjectFrame
units.summary: Assign the next frame selector from the first script parameter.

units.name: ObjectScriptReturnAndCall
units.summary: Command $8C installs the one saved return pointer as the script base and resets its cursor. Command $8D overwrites that saved pointer with the current base plus the already advanced cursor, then transfers to its parameter pointer. This is a single return slot, not a recursive call stack; uninitialized return state has no supported continuation.

units.name: SpawnChildObject
units.summary: Allocate a child while preserving the parent interpreter state. On success, place it relative to the parent and copy facing and X velocity; on failure, optionally take the command-supplied fallback pointer. Child offsets are signed.

units.name: PlaceChildVerticalPositive
units.summary: Positive vertical-offset fragment of child placement. The vertical high-byte carry propagation follows at FinishChildVerticalHigh.

units.name: PlaceChildVerticalNegative
units.summary: Negate the signed vertical offset, subtract it from the parent position and propagate borrow into the child's vertical high byte.

units.name: ObjectScriptLoopsAndTests
units.summary: Command $90 decrements the eight-bit per-object loop count first. A zero result continues at the current cursor; any nonzero result reinstalls the saved absolute loop pointer with cursor zero. A starting count of zero therefore wraps to $FF. The pointer/count must have been initialized; this routine does not validate them.

units.name: SetScriptPriorityAndDispatch
units.summary: One entry sets the script priority threshold. Another resolves a subcommand through ten paired targets and jumps indirectly. Only subcommands zero through nine have established flag-editing handlers; the full natural operand domain remains unresolved.

units.name: ClearObjectFacingFlags
units.summary: Clear the upper two facing/control bits of the indexed object.

units.name: JumpObjectScript
units.summary: Replace both the interpreter pointer and the per-slot saved stream pointer, then reset the byte cursor. A/Y hold low/high bytes at the shared entry.

units.name: SetCurrentScriptSelector
units.summary: Store the supplied selector without immediately replacing the stream pointer.

units.name: ApproachHorizontalSpeed
units.summary: Mirror the speed limits for negative motion, approach the lower limit by one, then apply direction-button acceleration or drag in steps of two. The adjustment now includes the negative-speed join; its signed limit bytes remain supplied by the script command.

units.name: PlayerMotionAndState
units.summary: Continue signed speed adjustment; right/left input accelerates toward the command limit, while drag reduces speed. Subsequent player-state logic handles transition state and falling below the visible playfield; its continuation is split by unknown bytes.

units.name: SelectPlayerAction
units.summary: Prioritize player state over directional input, handle temporary palette/animation slots and action-button state, then dispatch the chosen action through a two-byte pointer table. Exact game names for every action remain unresolved; numeric action values are retained where unsupported.

units.name: PlayerConditionalAction
units.summary: Check player flags and interaction state before a helper call; classified continuation ends before the decision completes.

units.name: SelectPlayerIdleScript
units.summary: Select script zero at priority zero through the shared script-selection routine.

units.name: SelectPlayerMovementScripts
units.summary: Three entry points select scripts five, one, or two with priorities zero, ten, or fifteen. Their exact animation names are not established.

units.name: SelectPlayerHighPriorityScript
units.summary: Select script eight with priority $BE through the common arbitration entry.

units.name: LatchPlayerAction
units.summary: Set the player action latch to one.

units.name: TestPlayerGrounded
units.summary: Return carry clear when the grounded/contact state is nonzero, set otherwise. Used as an object-script predicate.

units.name: HalveHorizontalVelocity
units.summary: Arithmetic right shift of the signed X velocity, preserving its sign bit in carry.

units.name: PlayerInputPredicates
units.summary: Consume the high-bit latch in the player countdown field, returning clear carry when consumed. A separate predicate returns carry set while the A button is held.

units.name: TestAndDampHorizontalVelocity
units.summary: Test whether signed velocity is small or agrees with facing. A separate predicate snaps speeds in the narrow zero neighborhood to zero and sets carry; larger speeds return without snapping.

units.name: PlayerWorldPredicates
units.summary: Test an area selector, or test proximity to the camera with an interaction override and A-button condition. A following entry clears the player transition state. Carry communicates the predicate result.

units.name: FindTypeTwoObject
units.summary: Scan nonplayer slots for type two, then reposition the indexed object relative to that object's X coordinate according to area. The positive-offset high-byte tail is not yet classified.

units.name: PlaceRelativeToTypeTwo
units.summary: Alternate placement uses X minus four and Y plus twenty-four from the type-two slot, propagating X borrow.

units.name: TestPlayerTransition
units.summary: Return carry set for a nonzero transition state, clear for zero.

units.name: FindSpecialObjectAndRecords
units.summary: Search nonplayer slots for type $35 or $33. A following path searches three-byte records matching the current coarse column and parity before invoking the record consumer. Record purpose is still tentative.

units.name: ConsumeMatchingSpawnRecord
units.summary: Alternate frames choose one of two record groups. Match column/parity and up to two area links; derive a distance count, stage placement fields and remove slot one before the position-transfer continuation completes the staged placement.

units.name: TestAreaCounter
units.summary: When the mode byte is below three, normalize the area index and test its low counter nibble; carry reports a nonzero counter. Otherwise return carry clear.

units.name: NormalizeAreaIndex
units.summary: Map area selectors at or above $30 down by $30 and return the resulting index in Y.

units.name: CaptureObjectMotionBias
units.summary: If the object's contact/classification flag is negative, copy its X velocity into the shared slot-zero motion bias.

units.name: ObjectGeometryPredicates
units.summary: Test contact state or the high byte of an X difference against the camera. A following fragment chooses facing toward slot zero using subtraction carry; callers must supply the incoming low-byte borrow convention.

units.name: ApplyVerticalAccelerationNegative
units.summary: For a negative nonzero Y velocity, increment it toward zero. The remaining acceleration paths follow in the next classified fragment.

units.name: ApplyVerticalAccelerationPositive
units.summary: Positive Y velocity increments up to $10; zero leaves the routine. The negative path increments again when its first increment reaches zero, so that path crosses zero instead of stopping there.

units.name: StopPlayerAgainstObject
units.summary: For flagged contacts, stop slot-zero X motion when it points into the indexed object. A following predicate returns carry clear when the object's classification flag is negative.

units.name: ChooseCameraScrollRate
units.summary: Convert the player's displacement from the camera to a clamped 32-entry index, with a fixed center index during transition state. Load direction and a two-byte scroll step from three 32-entry arrays. The clamped index and unconditional nonzero branch establish the boundary; these bytes are Data in the current map.

units.name: InitializeAndScrollNametables
units.summary: Initialize a nametable row/column and sprite-zero position from A; rendering must be disabled while direct PPU writes occur. The next routine advances or reverses the camera and fractional scroll accumulator, clamps underflow, and regenerates a column only when the coarse position changes.

units.name: ResetAndHardwareServices
units.summary: Reset waits for PPU readiness, disables rendering, resets MMC1 serial state, sets banks and clears internal RAM. Subsequent entries initialize the display, palettes/upload state, nametables, frame waits and five-bit mapper serial writes. Mapper register values are not physical bank identities.

units.name: CompareHighScore
units.summary: Compare six score digits from most significant index downward. If the current score exceeds the saved score, copy the digits; the classified copy loop ends before its branch tail.

units.name: QueueScoreDisplay
units.summary: Preserve the PRG selector, update the saved score, queue the label and convert stored digits to character tiles in reverse index order. The high bit terminates the final tile for the text queue helper.

units.name: RunGameplayFrameAndRasterSplit
units.summary: Main frame loop updates scroll, scripts, movement, rendering, audio and hooks, then waits for NMI acknowledgement. Transition flags end the loop unless priority sounds delay exit. The raster routine waits for sprite-zero hit, writes two timed palettes, restores scroll and switches CHR bank; instruction timing is intentional.

units.name: GameplayPauseReturn
units.summary: Return when the pause/input conditions skip the pause loop, or after its resume handshake finishes.

units.name: NmiAndUploadQueueWriter
units.summary: NMI preserves registers, optionally performs OAM DMA, handles scrolling column/upload/palette work, restores scroll/CHR and samples controllers; it clears the frame handshake and decrements timers. The later queue writer stores PPU address, count, mode and payload in page one, which is also CPU stack memory.

units.name: DrainUploadsAndWritePalettes
units.summary: Use page-one stack pulls to drain committed upload records until $FF, restoring the caller stack afterward. Mode selects vertical increment or unrolled sixteen-byte chunks. Following entries upload full or partial palettes and a new scrolling tile/attribute column.

units.name: SceneEntryWithFade
units.summary: Preserve the scene flags across fade setup, then choose the default or flagged scene entry. Its fixed-bank wait/setup continuation is now explained separately, including the Start-or-timeout loop.

units.name: InitializeDefaultScene
units.summary: Load scene descriptor one, then continue through display upload/readiness setup and a 120-tick presentation delay.

units.name: DispatchSceneFlags
units.summary: Use flag $20 to invoke the transition/fade sequence before continuing the scene dispatcher.

units.name: SelectSceneSequence
units.summary: Flag $80 selects an alternate sequence; otherwise use the continuation state or play scene records zero, one and two before text/palette sequencing. Only the beginning of this sequence is classified.

units.name: ClearSceneAndFade
units.summary: Fade down, synchronize with frames, disable rendering and hide sprites. Another entry stops audio and clears scroll/gameplay mode for a fresh scene.

units.name: ResumeSceneSequence
units.summary: Start scene record zero, then continue into the fixed scene/text presentation sequence.

units.name: AlternateSceneSequence
units.summary: Start scene record four with bit seven set, which suppresses the later input-wait prompt.

units.name: AnimateSceneAndWait
units.summary: Service raster frames and audio, seed a palette animation from frame bits, and request sound on a state flag. The following fragment handles exit conditions and controller shortcuts.

units.name: SceneInputExit
units.summary: Wait for sound completion or selected button combinations, then stop audio and service one more frame. Preserve the selected button flags in A across the return.

units.name: SetSceneContinuation
units.summary: Copy password success into the scene continuation state and begin the fade/transition sequence.

units.name: ServiceRasterFrame
units.summary: One entry services twice through fall-through. Mark a frame pending, delay, perform the raster split, and wait for NMI to clear the handshake.

units.name: WaitRasterFrames
units.summary: A supplies a countdown decremented by NMI; service raster and audio until it reaches zero.

units.name: LoadSceneAndUploadDescriptor
units.summary: Hide the OAM page and enable DMA. The scene loader switches to PRG register zero, reads a descriptor with two optional nametable payload selectors, CHR selector and palette selectors, then sequences direct uploads and fades. The upload routine supports raw lengths and a sentinel-selected packed stream.

units.name: DecodePackedPpuStream
units.summary: Packed stream commands: zero terminates, positive count copies that many literals, negative count repeats the following byte after masking bit seven ($80 wraps the byte counter for 256 repeats). Restore PPU state and PRG selector on exit. The descriptor loader supplies bank, length and source pointer plus optional destination.

units.name: BankedPaletteWrappers
units.summary: Preserve the active PRG register around palette initialization or fade steps in PRG pair zero. Return the palette routine's A result while restoring the original bank.

units.name: FadeAndSceneTextSequence
units.summary: Initialize fade counter to $FC, step fades with frame/audio service, and compose scene text from four-byte records. Queue the continue prompt unless bit seven suppresses it, then wait for both button press and release.

units.name: PulseSceneTextPalette
units.summary: Alternate two palette entries across two serviced frames, then darken both entries to $0F.

units.name: AudioRequestAndBankWrappers
units.summary: Stop both audio groups, or accept a new request only when its priority meets the current request. Bit seven marks restart pending. Banked audio update selects PRG register five and restores six afterward; sound identities remain numeric.

units.name: InitializeSpriteEngine
units.summary: Disable DMA while clearing OAM and object rendering state, then enable it again. The object initializer resolves a graphics resource and stages world/screen coordinates with optional coarse-column conversion; a negative return means allocation failed.

units.name: FinishObjectGraphicsInit
units.summary: Set Y, clear velocity and renderer state, or mark the resource selector invalid on failure. This is a continuation of the resource initialization routine, not an independent calling contract.

units.name: SelectCompatibleChrResource
units.summary: Resolve the requested resource descriptor and inspect constraints of active objects to find a compatible bank.

units.name: FindReusableObjectPalette
units.summary: Search the four cached palette slots for the requested value, then for a cache value unused by all eight objects. Failure leaves the previous selection; an available slot falls through to InstallObjectPaletteTriple, which replaces the cached descriptor and three colors.

units.name: RenderObjectMetasprites
units.summary: Finish a palette cache match and provide object removal. Build a compact list of renderable slots, then expand each object's frame into page-seven OAM. Packed dimensions control row/column traversal, $FF skips empty tiles, facing mirrors X traversal and attributes; offscreen tiles are clipped using high bytes.

units.name: BankTwoServiceWrappers
units.summary: Service HUD uploads, audio or generic queue writes through fixed-bank helpers, restoring PRG register two after each call.

units.name: BuildAndCompareObjectBounds
units.summary: Resolve frame-specific four-byte hitbox records in PRG register four, mirror X bounds when facing left, and form screen-space rectangles. The comparison uses a cheap X-distance rejection then strict overlap on both axes. Later code alternates collision candidates by frame parity and stages a response by object type.

units.name: NextCollisionCandidate
units.summary: Continue the alternating candidate loop down to slot one; the response body between classified fragments is unknown.

units.name: TickObjectCollisionTimers
units.summary: Skip during column transitions, then decrement the first nonzero high-nibble per-object timer. The tail of its side effect is not classified.

units.name: SelectTypeNineteenContact
units.summary: Search type-$19 objects, using alternating-frame selection when several exist; clear the selected contact field before the contact-resolution continuation handles matching object classes.

units.name: ResetAndFindObjectSupports
units.summary: Clear high-bit contact marks on all objects. A following routine scans active visible supports unless the player is transitioning; type $33 has an additional helper outside classified source.

units.name: MarkSupportOverlap
units.summary: Test the player's position within an object's vertical band and a 22-pixel horizontal window; set the object's high contact bit on overlap. Follow-on player adjustments are outside this fragment.

units.name: SupportLoopReturn
units.summary: Advance the support scan and restore the current object index before returning.

units.name: ChooseObjectAudio
units.summary: Keep selected priority sounds, otherwise stop sounds no longer owned by an active object. Scan object requests to select replacements; the continuation falls through to area-based background requests.

units.name: ChooseAreaAudio
units.summary: Finish scanning object sound requests. If none remain, select an area-dependent sound unless a player transition requires silence, using stop-then-restart to replace the current request.

units.name: UpdateSpawnsAndDespawn
units.summary: Cull objects in a rotating slot, handle a special type-two spawn, age three state arrays one index per frame, and update column-based spawn records. This is gameplay spawning, not proof of natural reachability of every record.

units.name: ColumnSpawnAndTileDecode
units.summary: Move a three-byte spawn-record cursor forward/backward, compare its coarse column, stage coordinates and spawn unless already active or suppressed. Subsequent code culls offscreen objects and builds a 24-tile scrolling column plus six attribute bytes from nested area/metatile tables.

units.name: UpdatePlayerAndWorld
units.summary: Dispatch player action, terrain resolution, object collisions and audio, then decrement the player latch. The world update services spawns, overlay, palette, scroll rate, area counters and object terrain checks. The final entry starts area-specific palette animation.

units.name: AnimateAreaPaletteAndHud
units.summary: Continue the timed area palette changes, including a branch comparing masked frame values with $0A/$0C that cannot match after AND #$07; preserve these original bytes. The HUD updater iterates pointer/destination pairs and queues two-row symbols when no upload is pending.

units.name: QueueTwoRowHudSymbol
units.summary: Map two symbol indices to top-row tiles, queue them, advance destination by 32 and map/queue bottom-row tiles. Commit the queue after both rows are present.

units.name: PreserveBankForAreaHelper
units.summary: Save the PRG register in shared scratch and switch to zero while preserving A. A paired entry restores it; nesting would overwrite the saved byte.

units.name: UpdateAreaCounterBanked
units.summary: Invoke the PRG-pair-zero per-area counter helper with the prior PRG register restored afterward.

units.name: InitializeFrameHooks
units.summary: Initialize four writable RAM callback pointers to the local RTS stub. Later scene-specific assignments may replace these defaults.

units.name: DispatchFrameHooks
units.summary: Four indirect jumps call writable RAM callbacks for NMI and frame phases. Targets depend on prior initialization; these instructions alone do not establish all target identities.

units.name: BankedSceneCallbacks
units.summary: Wrap password-screen or scene-palette callbacks with PRG register four, then restore six. The standalone RTS is a shared no-op hook.

units.name: ResolvePlayerTerrain
units.summary: Switch to PRG register four, sample terrain, align player Y to flat or slope surfaces and mark grounded state. Scan sampled tile flags for interaction/hazard classes; exact class names are not established. Transition paths use a reduced sample set.

units.name: FinishPlayerTerrain
units.summary: Combine terrain flags into sprite attributes, resample hazards, and preserve the prior grounded state if a blocking edge is encountered. The missing middle contains position restoration and needs separate classification.

units.name: SavePlayerPosition
units.summary: Save grounded state, then cache the player's X low/high and Y bytes for collision rollback.

units.name: SampleTerrainAndObjectGround
units.summary: Sample either a two-by-two or two-by-three tile footprint around the player, handling offscreen bounds. Resolve coarse map cells to per-tile collision flags using sixteen-byte records. A world-coordinate helper switches banks and clips bounds. The object loop snaps falling objects to flat/slope ground or removes them for flagged terrain. The policy/slope bytes beginning $F851 are Data in the current map; their semantic split and full selector domains remain unresolved.

units.name: ReadControllers
units.summary: Strobe both standard controller ports, then shift eight serial bits into each held-button byte. Result bits are A=$80, B=$40, Select=$20, Start=$10, Up=$08, Down=$04, Left=$02, Right=$01. No edge detector is implied by this sampler.

units.name: RandomAndTextQueue
units.summary: Seed and step a two-byte XOR/rotate pseudo-random state. The text reader walks address-prefixed, high-bit-terminated tile strings until a negative address-high sentinel; each string is queued via the page-one upload writer, then its final tile has bit seven cleared.

units.name: LoadAreaResourcePointers
units.summary: Double A to select paired pointers in nine tables and install resource bases in zero-page $AB..$BC. These include spawn/script families, frame/width and CHR-compatibility columns. Independent six-cell table boundaries are supported; natural area selection and some original resource names remain unresolved.

units.name: HandleContactTileRange23
units.summary: Check three sampled tile IDs for $23..$2C, retain the matching sample coordinate and convert the ID to a zero-based selector. Clear its map cell, request sound $12 and enter the associated fixed-bank transition helper. The command-processing continuation follows at ProcessSceneStripCommand.

units.name: ToggleContactTileAndQueueStrip
units.summary: Check three tile samples for $2D..$32. Toggle bit seven of the corresponding six-entry state, choose a replacement tile, then either save its low selector or toggle the companion state and request animation. The following helper derives a nametable strip from a descriptor, queues repeated tile bytes, and marks uploads pending; the coordinate helper converts screen coordinates to a PPU address.

units.name: ResolveMapRowCell
units.summary: Resolve a cell pointer from row tables $E3DC/$E3FC, with the column offset reduced by two. Returns the CPU pointer in $07/$08; those tables describe RAM rows, not contiguous ROM records.

units.name: AnimateContactTilePairs
units.summary: Every seventh tick, when enabled and neither side has a tile in $0B..$22, remap eligible IDs one through four at up to two sampled cells. Update RAM and queue the matching nametable byte, avoiding a duplicate update when both coordinates match.

units.name: AnimateSixTileStrips
units.summary: Scan six animation slots. Negative counters disable a slot; each expiry reloads two and advances an eight-phase index. Companion state selects one of two eight-byte phase sets before the strip upload helper runs.

units.name: ReplaceMetatileAtPosition
units.summary: Entry variants accept packed cell coordinates directly or derive them from X/Y screen position. Resolve the metatile descriptor, merge its palette quadrant into the attribute byte after synchronizing with NMI, then request replacement of the four tiles. Map writes require valid packed/map coordinates and a RAM-backed destination. These local Static calling preconditions support the connected code; natural callers maintaining them remain unresolved.

units.name: MetatileReplacementReturn
units.summary: Return without replacement when coordinate validation fails.

units.name: ValidateCoordinatesAndBuildMetatileUpload
units.summary: Reject screen positions outside the interior rows/columns and pack a cell coordinate. Derive attribute address and quadrant shift from that coordinate, read descriptor byte four, and prepare upload commands. The one-byte queue writer emits address, length, increment mode, tile and terminator; the replacement path also tests occupied RAM cells before writing two rows and collision metadata.

units.name: QueueMetatileRowOrReject
units.summary: Reject an occupied replacement with A=0. The row writer queues two descriptor bytes at the prepared PPU address, advances Y to the next row and leaves the upload cursor at the terminator.

units.name: WriteMetatileCollisionAndResolveDescriptor
units.summary: Copy a four-byte collision descriptor into two RAM map rows. The next entry resolves graphics pointer tables and a four-byte collision record from the metatile selector in Y; it leaves graphics and collision pointers in scratch.

units.name: QueueThreeDecimalDigits
units.summary: Convert the unsigned byte in A to three digit tiles by repeated subtraction of 100 then 10. Queue three bytes at the X/Y PPU address; leading zeroes are retained as tile $30.

units.name: ObjectBoundsAndSceneState
units.summary: Build facing-aware object rectangles from four-byte descriptors and test overlap against the saved player rectangle, returning A=0/1. The player-only entry saves that rectangle. Following scene passes suppress displayed frame selectors from visibility/control flags, update an eight-frame countdown, mask working palettes according to scene flags, and conditionally replace a metatile when scene selectors match. Exact game names of scene flags remain unresolved.

units.name: ReplaceSceneTileOnCounterMatch
units.summary: Compare a scene-dependent threshold against the player counter before requesting replacement metatile $0D. Zero replacement coordinates skip the request; ResetSceneCommandSequence supplies the connected transition/reset tail.

units.name: SceneTileCheckReturn
units.summary: Shared return for failed scene-selector or counter tests.

units.name: TickSceneTimerAndInteractions
units.summary: Queue the scene timer on alternate frames and decrement it on its divider while active. Expiry either enters the fixed transition path or marks the alternate scene mode and requests sound. The interaction pass tests B-button edges and prioritized sampled tile IDs, selecting either a metatile replacement or the separate removal path. Full game identities of the tile IDs remain unresolved.

units.name: RemoveInteractionTile
units.summary: Convert the selected contact coordinate to a PPU/map address, clear its RAM cell and invoke the fixed-bank update with a one-byte zero payload. The connected transition request continues at RequestSceneTransitionEleven.

units.name: FindContactTileAndReplaceObjectCell
units.summary: Search three sampled tile IDs for A, returning carry set and the matching coordinate in Y. The next entry uses a saved object slot to replace the cell at its horizontal center with metatile $82; invalid slot values skip it.

units.name: SceneCountdownAndPaletteCycle
units.summary: Clear the saved replacement-object slot. Separate updates alternate a countdown and script-selector frame-copying window, and cycle four palette colors every seven ticks in the ordinary scene mode. Exact gameplay names of these effects remain tentative.

units.name: OpenInventoryOverlay
units.summary: Save the overlay entry mode, disable object rendering, enable OAM transfer and write CHR selector $13. The aligned MMC1 serializer writes only CHR0, preserving PRG banks 8/9 for InitializePasswordOverlay. Natural serializer alignment is a local entry precondition.

units.name: InventoryOverlayActionEntry
units.summary: Shared no-op return and pending-selection entry; a latched selection invokes the overlay toggle helper before continuation outside this run.

units.name: MoveInventoryCursorAndSwapItems
units.summary: Negative mode exits immediately. Otherwise toggle row state or interpret Select/A/Start actions, wrap left/right cursor within the current item count, redraw it, and swap entries while selection is latched. Each swap redraws the old and new positions; the continuation restores the saved selection from the matching stack push before redrawing.

units.name: LatchInventorySelection
units.summary: Return from cursor processing, or latch the current entry and draw its selected marker. An already latched entry takes the clearing path.

units.name: ClearInventorySelection
units.summary: Clear the selection latch and redraw the ordinary entry marker. The adjacent return now completes this path without additional mutation.

units.name: DrawInventorySelectionMarker
units.summary: Choose one of two OAM marker records, fill its tile and horizontal position from the selected item, and build a one-row upload at $21xx. The rendering helper consumes the scratch source/address fields. The continuation increments the upload/display latch and returns.

units.name: EraseInventorySelectionMarker
units.summary: Hide the selected OAM marker with Y=$F0, derive its item column and tail-call the shared upload setup to restore the entry tile.

units.name: FindPasswordMismatchPartner
units.summary: Save the mismatch index, scan forward in the entered buffer until the expected byte appears again, save that second index and return A=0. The paired password records provide the permutation precondition. Following entries filter button repeat and draw the overlay cursor.

units.name: TestInventoryFlag
units.summary: Resolve the low six bits of A to a bit mask and byte index, then test the corresponding zero-page flag byte at $E0+X. Returns the masked flag in A.

units.name: ResolveInventoryFlagMask
units.summary: Use low three selector bits to fetch a one-bit mask and the remaining three bits as byte index X. Selectors alias modulo 64 intentionally.

units.name: BuildOverlaySpriteSequence
units.summary: Initialize three sprite groups and two moving boundaries. Subsequent entries move those boundaries by four toward fixed limits, adjust sprite priority, and queue three short rows of overlay text. Shared upload helper advances source by three bytes and destination by one nametable row; source-page carry continuation is separately classified.

units.name: AdvanceOverlayTextRow
units.summary: Advance the upload destination by $20 after the source pointer step. Only the low destination byte changes in this fragment, as required by the caller's bounded rows.

units.name: TestOverlayEffectSelector
units.summary: Branch on the saved effect selector; the zero-selector path between classified fragments remains unresolved.

units.name: InitializeOverlayEffectPalette
units.summary: Clear effect state, assign the effect's working colors and queue its initialization descriptor through the fixed-bank upload wrapper.

units.name: DispatchOverlayEffect
units.summary: Save Y as effect selector. A bit seven increments an audio/control counter, bit six requests sound $33, and the low three bits select a bank-local indirect handler. Six paired targets support effects zero through five. Despite the three-bit mask, apparent entries six/seven target RAM $0341/$0002 and are outside this ROM-handler contract.

units.name: RunDiagonalSpriteEffect
units.summary: Initialize the effect and its sprite groups, then repeatedly move visible sprites diagonally and advance animation while servicing a frame. A selector-dependent interval controls the repeat; the middle coordinate adjustment remains outside this classified run.

units.name: CheckDiagonalEffectThreshold
units.summary: Compare the sprite coordinate against the selector-specific threshold and repeat the effect interval while it has not crossed the endpoint.

units.name: InitializeAndMoveEffectSprites
units.summary: Build three sprite groups from selector-dependent coordinates. The movement entry walks OAM records $90..$FC, skips hidden sprites and moves visible sprites up one/right one. The following animation entry decrements its delay and selects a frame-dependent pacing mask; the phase-mask branch selects the existing animation continuation.

units.name: AdvanceEffectAnimationPhase
units.summary: On eligible frame ticks, hide the first sixteen sprites while preserving the anchor, place up to four successive animation frames and advance phase. At delay expiry, restart phase only after the moving sprite crosses the vertical threshold; selectors determine the next delay.

units.name: RunTwoDigitOverlayAnimation
units.summary: Load selector-specific two-digit values and count. Draw both sprite digits, service a selector-dependent number of frames while fading their palette, advance the decimal pair with carry at ten, and repeat until the count expires. The draw helper positions two sprite groups at adjacent horizontal anchors.

units.name: FadeOverlayDigitPalette
units.summary: Use a selector-dependent frame mask to pace three palette entries. Subtract one brightness step and wrap underflow within the palette range; leave entry zero untouched.

units.name: RunSimpleOverlayDelay
units.summary: Initialize effect descriptor $0B then wait the number of frames held in the effect selector.

units.name: RunOverlayFlashAndPaletteSequence
units.summary: Run eight cycles of three sprite frames, hiding old OAM before each frame. The following entry toggles CHR state, alternates palette fills and waits, requests sound $25 and finishes with a longer hold. Helpers fill all 32 colors, preserve one emphasis color and route delays through the bank-restoring wrapper.

units.name: AudioParameterPitchIndex
units.summary: Read the audio command parameter, add the slot's base index, resolve a pitch lookup value and store it. Reaching the slot threshold changes the modulation mode to $A0; the continuation below threshold is already explained in adjacent source.

units.name: AdvanceAudioModulationAccumulator
units.summary: Unless modulation bit six disables updates, add the instrument-dependent step to the accumulator. Negative modulation mode selects the subtracting/clamping path; other modes continue through the previously classified audio update.

units.name: ClampDescendingAudioModulation
units.summary: Subtract the accumulated modulation offset from the threshold value and compare with the current slot value. Equality or underflow follows adjacent classified clamps; larger values reach the shared output store.

units.name: StoreAudioModulationOutput
units.summary: Store the computed modulation output in the shared audio scratch byte and return. The unindexed store is intentional.

units.name: FinishUpperAudioSlotPass
units.summary: Process a slot through the audio interpreter, then descend through slot four before entering the common upper-group cleanup.

units.name: InitializeObjectSlots
units.summary: Run the shared object reset helper, then mark all eight object-type entries inactive with $FF.

units.name: ObjectPredicateReturn
units.summary: Return from the object predicate path whose decision is explained in the adjacent reviewed code.

units.name: MarkObjectPaletteControl
units.summary: Return from the preceding object path, or set bit seven of the indexed palette selector/control byte. Facing selects the shared continuation.

units.name: ExecuteObjectScriptAndYield
units.summary: Invoke the object interpreter entry, set its result to $FF and return. This explicitly yields the caller's command processing.

units.name: FinishChildVerticalHigh
units.summary: Propagate the low-Y carry into the parent's vertical high byte and store it in child slot Y. The low-byte and index setup are in adjacent reviewed source.

units.name: TestObjectTerrainCounter
units.summary: Start with carry set and test the indexed terrain counter. Zero returns immediately; the nonzero path's carry adjustment is separately classified.

units.name: SampleObjectCenterTerrain
units.summary: Return from the counter predicate, or sample terrain at the object's horizontal center and current Y. The special $FF result takes the carry-clear exit; the intervening alternative remains outside this classified fragment.

units.name: TurnObjectAtTerrainBoundary
units.summary: Return carry clear for the empty sample. The next entry samples two facing-dependent points beside the object: incompatible terrain clears horizontal velocity and flips both upper facing bits. Samples use the shared terrain reader and preserve exact signed/unsigned byte arithmetic.

units.name: ObjectActionNoOpReturn
units.summary: Shared return for an object action with no further state change in this classified suffix.

units.name: DispatchPlayerDirectionAction
units.summary: Skip inactive, special-state or inhibited players. Mirror horizontal direction bits when facing is negative, retain the low input nibble and dispatch through split low/high address tables. The sixteen masked action targets are now classified and named. Valid coordinates and the handlers' local contracts support these static paths; no natural calling invariant is inferred.

units.name: AttachPlayerToSupportingObject
units.summary: Reset player script/control state through the common selector. The support search scans active object slots one through seven with the required type flags, checks a narrow vertical interval and horizontal overlap, saves the support slot and copies its two fractional coordinates into the player before clearing player state.

units.name: UpdateObjectTypeHandlers
units.summary: Run the object/audio arbitration pass, then scan object slots seven down to one. Skip frozen or inactive entries, save current slot and call its type handler. Types 0..86 form the supported finite Static handler domain. This does not establish that every natural object-type writer remains in that domain or that arbitrary map writes preserve the mapper.

units.name: DispatchObjectTypeHandler
units.summary: Continue the descending object loop; resolve the object type through split pointer tables and jump indirectly through scratch $39/$3A.

units.name: SpawnWithFacingDependentParameters
units.summary: Save caller slot and spawn parameters. Choose the horizontal parameter according to facing, set its companion to $F8 and call the allocator with policy one. The connected continuation returns zero on failure or initializes the child frame and position before returning one.

units.name: ArbitrateObjectAudioCues
units.summary: Unless the shared pause/inhibit byte is set, count type-one objects, those with nonzero high X or Y and those with flag eight. Stop cues $19/$1A when no eligible difference remains; otherwise choose $19 or $1A from the remaining object flags, avoiding repeated requests for the current cue.

units.name: RecordPlayerStateRunsInNametable
units.summary: Only in scene mode two, combine facing bits and current player action into a byte. Track runs of that state with a byte counter; start a new two-byte PPU record when the state changes or the counter reaches $FF. The address wraps from $26EE to $2400 at the explicit boundary. Exact higher-level recording purpose remains tentative.

units.name: InitializeAreaDisplayAndAttributes
units.summary: Disable/synchronize rendering through fixed helpers, initialize the area and read both 64-byte attribute tables through buffered PPUDATA into RAM. Copy incoming area/camera fields, load the area descriptor, clear initial coordinate scratch and start camera clamping.

units.name: ComputeInitialCameraOffset
units.summary: Subtract four from the bounded incoming area position; underflow correction occupies a separately classified boundary. The following run scales the adjusted coordinate by 32.

units.name: InitializeCameraAndMapColumns
units.summary: Scale the camera cell coordinate into a 16-bit pixel position, copy it to camera and player staging fields, derive its column index and initialize the map/nametable columns. Clear raster CHR state and restore display/audio helpers before returning.

units.name: BeginAreaNametableLoad
units.summary: Disable PPU NMI generation and select the area-loading variant with Y=1. This takes the shared nonzero branch to the resource loader.

units.name: LoadAreaGraphicsResources
units.summary: Load graphics resources through the shared Y=1 upload; alternate entry accepts descriptor $16 before shared $18 nametable initialization.

units.name: BuildInitialVisibleColumns
units.summary: Save PPU control, enable vertical increment and walk 64 columns starting sixteen columns before the camera. Skip negative positions; derive nametable and attribute addresses, load map-column data, render it, clear allocation inhibit and service the fixed update. The stack preserves the loop counter around helpers.

units.name: FinishInitialColumnPass
units.summary: Restore the loop counter and repeat all 64 columns, then restore both PPU control shadow and hardware register.

units.name: InitializeSceneAndGameplay
units.summary: Clear five low-RAM scene fields, reset frame hooks and rendering, initialize the banked object layer, clear pause/transition flags and call area setup. Subsequent fixed continuation is classified separately.

units.name: TestSceneInventoryFlag
units.summary: Test the flag selector in Y through the bank-restoring wrapper. Zero takes the scene fallback search; the nonzero continuation lies between classified fragments.

units.name: SearchSceneFlagSelectors
units.summary: Search selectors $27 down through $1E for a clear inventory flag. A match enters the already reviewed scene setup; exhausting the range jumps to scene completion.

units.name: EnterSceneCompletionSequence
units.summary: Call the scene completion setup, display helpers and ending/presentation sequence. Banked continuation after that sequence is not inferred here.

units.name: InitializeCurrentArea
units.summary: Clear input and camera transition state, initialize objects and audio, select an area resource family from the high nibble of incoming area selector, then load area display, install ordinary frame hooks, initialize the initial frames and enter gameplay.

units.name: PrimeSevenGameplayFrames
units.summary: Prime seven frames with NMI synchronization. Each frame sets pending, performs a bounded CPU delay, resets the descending frame byte, runs object update/render helpers and waits for NMI acknowledgement before advancing the count.

units.name: CopyEightUploadPayloadBytes
units.summary: Unrolled continuation copies eight successive bytes from the upload source into the page-one command queue, advancing both cursors. Command header and tail handling remain explained in the surrounding reviewed uploader.

units.name: RunScenePresentationList
units.summary: Prepare the presentation, wait and request sound, then read paired entries from a PRG-pair-four list until its zero terminator. Restore PRG pair six for each effect and frame wait. After the list, request the closing cue, invoke the final effect and enter the shared presentation completion sequence.

units.name: RunPresentationCompletion
units.summary: Initialize presentation state, service audio and sprites until the animated boundaries meet, then optionally scroll the raster by four to $80 and draw three paired values as successive rows. Palette changes at the exact anchor and bounded counters control timing. The final section requests the completion cue; later continuation remains separately classified.

units.name: JoinPresentationWait
units.summary: Jump to the shared presentation wait path; this is a control-flow bridge, not an independent animation.

units.name: WaitPresentationFrames
units.summary: Store A as frame countdown and service frame/audio until the shared countdown reaches zero. Callers must use the established NMI ticking path.

units.name: InitializePresentationPalette
units.summary: Mark palette initialization active, synchronize a frame, load the requested descriptor and copy 32 target colors into the working palette. Service audio/palette helpers and clear the active flag after setup.

units.name: ClearObjectHorizontalHigh
units.summary: Clear the indexed object's horizontal high coordinate. This is the missing branch tail of the adjacent object-position helper.

units.name: StoreObjectRenderCount
units.summary: Store A into the indexed object render-count/control field and return. The caller supplies its value.

units.name: StoreObjectPaletteSelector
units.summary: Store A into the indexed palette selector/control field and return. Adjacent alternate entries supply the value.

units.name: InstallObjectPaletteTriple
units.summary: Save the selected palette descriptor per group, scale descriptor and destination indices by four, copy three colors into the working palette, then restore the current object index.

units.name: RunGameplayHooksAndInteractions
units.summary: The first frame pass updates player input/terrain and object handlers, switches to PRG pair two for scene effects, then restores PRG pair six. The second pass services interaction tiles, scene timers, palettes, contact effects, support and object scripts before committing uploads and saving prior player coordinates/input. NMI-side helpers write state-run bytes, read seven PPU sample pairs and read or commit the pending attribute byte. Object overlap handling selects special player states or the shared failure path; tile $22 records its area bit and freezes object updates. Each bank switch shown is explicit; indirect callees retain unresolved bank contracts.

units.name: HandlePlayerFailureAndPendingSceneAction
units.summary: Check hazard tile $1A, consume the pending scene selector, detect a nonzero horizontal high byte and request transition, or set the failure state and script $0B before clearing matching transient objects. Branches preserve the current bank's supported contract.

units.name: DispatchPlayerSecondaryAction
units.summary: The wrapper switches to PRG pair six for player failure and restores PRG pair two. The action entry detects a new B press against prior input, resolves a nonzero action selector through a local pointer table and calls the indirect trampoline. Target meanings are only known where independently classified.

units.name: ClearTransientTypeZeroObjects
units.summary: Scan slots one through seven. Convert active type-zero objects to inactive $80, update their render-count/control byte and clear the shared secondary-action selector when such an object is removed.

units.name: GameplayResourceAndTerrainPasses
units.summary: Consume remaining scene timer units with synchronized frames, updating its display and audio. A separate entry searches for an existing active type-zero object before spawning a selector-dependent object. Other entries release the player's transition lock after crossing a tile boundary, collect center/edge terrain samples with matching RAM/PPU coordinates, and dispatch by player action through split pointer tables. The seventeen finite terrain response entries are now classified. Their local valid-coordinate/RAM-map contracts are explicit; exact gameplay identities and natural selector bounds remain unresolved.

units.name: SamplePlayerSidesAndAlignToTerrain
units.summary: Align the player to an eight-pixel vertical boundary when contact permits, clear motion state and start tile animation. Sample three heights on each side and restore prior X when terrain IDs $0E/$11/$12 obstruct motion. The common bounds helper derives top/middle/bottom sample points; the reader converts pixels to RAM row/column, returns tile $0E outside columns 0..27 and masks valid map cells to six bits.

units.name: SpawnFromThreeByteSceneRecord
units.summary: Multiply the record selector by three, resolve the scene-specific record pointer, adjust its first byte against scene thresholds, and pass its two spawn parameters to the PRG-pair-six allocator. Restore PRG pair two, then copy the third record byte into the allocated object's flags.

units.name: SpawnTimedSceneObject
units.summary: Only in scene mode two, compare the scene timer against the next of seven event thresholds. Convert the packed position into spawn coordinates, spawn record two, clear the new object's script and per-slot event field and advance the event index.

units.name: UnpackSceneSpawnPosition
units.summary: Convert A's low nibble to horizontal pixels and its high nibble plus $0F to vertical position, storing the allocator's staging coordinates.

units.name: SpawnInitialPlayerFromRecord
units.summary: Select a four-byte initial-player record, install its X/Y staging coordinates, clear the spawn control field and tail-call allocation into slot zero with the record's resource/script selectors.

units.name: ClearAreaSpawnScratch
units.summary: Clear two scratch fields and allocation state, then zero the 86-byte area spawn scratch array. This establishes the subsequent column/spawn initialization baseline.

units.name: LoadTwelveByteAreaDescriptor
units.summary: Scale the incoming selector to a twelve-byte record at bank-three $BA92. Read map/resource pointers, CHR selector, source bank and rendering parameters. Copy $DE bytes of resource data from PRG pair five into RAM, switch to the descriptor's map bank and consume its nine-byte header before advancing the remaining map stream pointer. The source-page carry is handled in the separately classified boundary.

units.name: InstallOrdinaryGameplayHooks
units.summary: Restore PRG pair six and return from descriptor loading. The ordinary initializer installs before/after render hooks, clears movement/spawn state, creates the initial player, positions it relative to the camera and incoming Y, then marks the initial scene state $80.

units.name: SetPlayerTransitionMarker
units.summary: When the compared action byte is $E6, assign transition marker $90; other values continue through the existing classified action path.

units.name: AddScoreWithRestoredPrgBank
units.summary: Save the PRG selector in $3B, select PRG pair zero and add the packed BCD input into six score digits. The score helper uses $2F..$34 and preserves $3B; the tail restores the original PRG selector. This is a static local bank/return contract.

units.name: LoadAreaResourcePointersWrapper
units.summary: Preserve A, switch to PRG pair zero, run the nine-pointer resource loader, then restore PRG pair six. This is an explicit return-bank contract.

units.name: SetFrameHookPointers
units.summary: Four entry points store A/X as low/high callback addresses for NMI PPU, NMI tail, before-render and after-render hooks. These RAM CPU addresses are execution targets, not physical ROM identities.

units.name: OpenOverlayAndInstallHooks
units.summary: Enter PRG pair four, call overlay setup and restore the gameplay bank. Install the overlay frame hooks afterwards; the setup callee's nested return behavior remains an explicit disassembly question.

units.name: BankFourEffectWrappers
units.summary: Six wrappers enter PRG pair four, invoke the effect dispatcher, sprite initializer, two boundary movers, finishing upload or final palette setup, and restore the incoming gameplay bank through the shared return helper.

units.name: QueueUploadAndRestoreOverlayBank
units.summary: Build the upload command in fixed code, then tail-call the PRG-pair-four entry wrapper so the overlay caller continues in its expected bank.

units.name: LoadResourceAndRestoreOverlayBank
units.summary: Load the requested resource through the fixed helper, then restore PRG pair four for the overlay continuation.

units.name: PresentationWaitAndFlagWrappers
units.summary: Initialize presentation palettes or wait frames in fixed code, restoring PRG pair four afterwards. A third wrapper enters PRG pair four to test a packed inventory flag and restores the gameplay bank before returning its result.

units.name: DrawPackedSpriteRectangle
units.summary: Save the incoming PRG bank, select graphics/CHR resources from Y, resolve the sprite record for A and decode packed row/column dimensions into doubled counts. Walk the rectangular tile grid in eight-pixel steps, omitting zero tiles from OAM, then walk emitted records backwards to assign the final attribute byte. Restore the incoming PRG bank and return A=1. X is the caller's OAM byte cursor; capacity and record validity are caller preconditions.

units.name: ToggleSceneTileState
units.summary: Toggle the contact tile's six-entry state and choose the replacement tile/animation path.

units.name: QueueAnimatedTileStrip
units.summary: Use the packed scene descriptor and active strip flags to derive a repeated-byte PPU upload.

units.name: QueueTileAtScreenCoordinate
units.summary: A is the tile, X/Y are screen coordinates. Convert to a nametable address and queue a single-byte update.

units.name: ReplaceMetatileAtPackedCell
units.summary: A is the packed cell coordinate and Y selects the replacement descriptor; share the synchronized replacement path.

units.name: ReplaceMetatileAtScreenPosition
units.summary: Validate and pack X/Y before preparing the replacement; invalid coordinates return without touching the map.

units.name: PrepareMetatileAttribute
units.summary: Derive $23C0-based attribute address and two-bit quadrant shift; descriptor byte four supplies palette bits.

units.name: QueueSingleNametableByte
units.summary: Append one tile at address X/Y to the page-one upload queue and mark graphics pending.

units.name: ReplaceFourMetatileTiles
units.summary: Resolve Y's descriptor, derive two nametable rows and collision cells from A, and reject occupied destinations when the caller requests that check.

units.name: QueueTwoMetatileTiles
units.summary: Append two bytes from the descriptor cursor at the prepared PPU address and advance both cursors.

units.name: ResolveMetatileResources
units.summary: Y selects split graphics pointers and a four-byte collision record. These are CPU pointers in the current bank contract.

units.name: ConvertByteToThreeDigits
units.summary: Return hundreds, tens and ones tile codes in scratch $3D..$3F; each digit includes tile base $30.

units.name: ExtractDecimalDigit
units.summary: Divide A by the divisor in X by repeated subtraction. Save remainder and return quotient plus tile base $30.

units.name: SavePlayerCollisionRectangle
units.summary: Build the player's facing-aware rectangle in scratch $3D..$40 for the subsequent object overlap tests.

units.name: ApplySceneObjectVisibility
units.summary: Reset displayed frame selectors and per-slot freeze flags according to scene state and object control bits, then tick the player-state timeout every eighth frame.

units.name: ApplyScenePaletteMask
units.summary: Copy sixteen target colors, then blank selected groups to the first color according to scene effect bits.

units.name: CheckSceneMetatileTrigger
units.summary: Compare current area/event selectors before requesting one of the scene's metatile replacements.

units.name: ProcessSceneInteractionTile
units.summary: New B presses prioritize explicit tile selectors; the passive checks use the scene mode flags. Exact tile game names remain unresolved.

units.name: ReplaceSavedObjectMetatile
units.summary: If the saved object slot is valid, use its center position to request replacement metatile $82.

units.name: TickSceneScriptWindow
units.summary: Alternate a timed selector-frame-copying window with a longer countdown; copy last frames into current frame selectors during the window.

units.name: CycleScenePaletteColors
units.summary: In the ordinary scene mode, cycle four colors at a seven-tick cadence in both target and working palettes.

units.name: ReadOverlayCursorInput
units.summary: Obtain repeated input, handle action buttons, wrap horizontal position and redraw selected buffer entries; these buffers also serve the password mode.

units.name: ToggleOverlaySelectionLatch
units.summary: Select and mark the current entry or clear the active selection latch.

units.name: DrawSecondOverlayMarker
units.summary: Alternate marker entry using the second four-byte OAM record.

units.name: EraseSecondOverlayMarker
units.summary: Alternate hide entry for the second OAM marker.

units.name: FilterOverlayButtonRepeat
units.summary: Decrement the repeat timer, shorten it on input changes, accept input at expiry and request the cursor cue. Otherwise clear the frame input byte.

units.name: DrawOverlayCursorSprites
units.summary: Choose row/column coordinates for either editable-buffer or grid mode, read OAM templates and hide unused records at their $FF terminator.

units.name: MoveOverlayBoundaryRight
units.summary: Advance the first boundary by four toward $BC and redraw its sprite group.

units.name: MoveOverlayBoundaryLeft
units.summary: Decrease the second boundary by four toward $A4 and redraw its sprite group eight pixels to the left.

units.name: FinishOverlaySpriteSequence
units.summary: Set priority on the sprite group and queue three short text rows before committing uploads.

units.name: QueueOverlayTextRow
units.summary: Queue a four-column row, advance the source by three bytes and move to the next PPU row.

units.name: MoveEffectSpritesDiagonally
units.summary: Walk OAM records from $90 to $FC; skip Y=$F0 and move visible sprites one pixel up/right.

units.name: TickEffectSpriteAnimation
units.summary: Count down the effect delay and pace the phase changes from the descending frame byte.

units.name: DrawTwoEffectDigits
units.summary: Render the two digit selectors at adjacent fixed horizontal anchors using separate OAM groups.

units.name: ReplaceOverlaySpriteFrame
units.summary: Hide all old OAM entries, then draw the selected frame at the shared anchor.

units.name: RunOverlayPaletteFlash
units.summary: Toggle CHR selection and alternate palette fills and delays; request sound $25 before the final hold.

units.name: WaitWithOverlayEmphasisColor
units.summary: Set the emphasis color and wait A frames through the bank-restoring wrapper.

units.name: BlankPaletteThenWait
units.summary: Fill all palette entries with $0F, then wait the caller's saved duration.

units.name: FillPaletteThenEmphasize
units.summary: Fill all palette entries with $30 and continue through the emphasis-delay helper.

units.name: FillWorkingPalette
units.summary: Fill all 32 working palette entries with A.

units.name: SetObjectPaletteHighFlag
units.summary: Set bit seven of the palette selector/control field, then select the facing-dependent tail from the object facing byte.

units.name: TestObjectCenterSample
units.summary: Sample terrain at object center, returning carry according to the $FF sentinel path.

units.name: ReverseObjectAtTerrainEdge
